seoDescription: TCP/IP in FPGA: MAC, ARP, IPv4 and a TCP state machine with retransmission, all in hardware with no soft core in the data path.

sections.heading: PURE-RTL TCP OFFLOAD ENGINE
sections.body: ZCU106 / SFP0 · NO PROCESSOR IN THE DATAPATH

images.alt: Two dithered hands meeting through a PROJECT.EXE window under the letters TCP/IP

sections.heading: $ cat README.md | head
sections.body: A TCP/IP stack implemented entirely in FPGA fabric. MAC, ARP, IPv4, the RFC 9293 state machine, retransmission, RTO estimation, congestion control and reassembly are all RTL.

sections.heading: THE STACK
sections.body:
application (echo | counter)
               │
       toe_tcp_engine     RFC 9293 FSM, cwnd,
               │          retransmit, reassembly
       toe_ip_bridge      header + RFC 1071 csum,
               │          double-buffered
         eth_ip_core      IPv4 + ARP + MAC
               │
     gig_ethernet_pcs_pma  SGMII
               │
      GTH Quad 225 ch2 ──▶ SFP0 cage

items.label: TX PATH
items.detail: The application writes into toe_send_buffer. On a flush the engine asks toe_segmenter for a segment bounded by cwnd, the peer window and free retransmission-table space. The bridge builds the header and computes the checksum while it reads, over a doubled buffer so segment N+1 is prepared while N is on the wire.

items.label: RX PATH
items.detail: The bridge parses inbound TCP, verifies the checksum and offers it to the engine. A one-deep skid buffer latches it the cycle it is offered, whatever the FSM state. Pure ACKs drain even while the FSM waits on a TX segment.

items.value: rtl/ 23 VHDL modules · rtl/eth/ 28 Verilog files · tb/ 49 testbenches · vectors/ 25 golden files

sections.heading: TWO MACS ON THE WIRE
sections.body:
00:0a:35 is the Xilinx OUI; bc:e9:2f is the host NIC. Two distinct MACs, not loopback. Taking the host link down mid-transfer halted the stream at once, and every source in build_toe.tcl greps clean for zynq_ultra_ps_e, processing_system and PS8.

Passive open now works too: 40 of 40 sequential inbound connections accepted.

sections.heading: THE THREE CHANGES
sections.body: Identify a variant by md5, never by filename. A bitstream believed to be step 2 was once step 2b; only the WNS gave it away.

items.label: Inline checksum.
items.detail: Start the checksum at accept time and feed it words as bytes arrive, overlapping the ~740-clock walk with the 1460-clock read.

items.label: Double buffering.
items.detail: Fill and send in separate processes over twice the buffer. One clock under line rate.

items.label: D21 RX starvation fix.
items.detail: Skid buffer, un-gated RX branch, in-freeze pure-ACK drain. Without it, step 2 reached 569 Mbps and killed the connection at 70–130 MB, every run.

items.label: Sustained throughput, 3.489 GB over 30 active s

sections.heading: WHAT THIS IS NOT
sections.body:
Single connection: no session table. RFC compliance measured on the wire is 10 PASS / 2 FAIL. Regression runs 46 pass / 2 fail / 1, both failures pre-existing on baseline RTL.

WIN_LIMIT is a deployment constant at 8192; raising it to 32768 changed nothing, because the board is the sender. Bouncing the host NIC can drop the SGMII carrier; budget one reflash after any link interruption.

sections.heading: NEXT // pl-tcp-stack-10g
sections.body: A 64-bit datapath on 10GBASE-R. Phase 2 of 5: tree and 10G substrate in progress, nothing widened yet. The 1G design closes at +0.225 ns over 237,022 endpoints at 8.000 ns; 156.25 MHz native means finding 1.6 ns.
